Role of the Crypto Driver in the Crypto Stack

The Crypto Driver is located in the Microcontroller Abstraction Layer below the Crypto Interface (CryIf) and Crypto Service Manager (CSM). It provides a generic interface for synchronous and asynchronous cryptographic primitives and handles key storage, key configuration, and key management. An ECU integrates exactly one CSM and one CryIf. However, the CryIf can address multiple Crypto Drivers SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15. The specification summarizes the service offering into two services: crypto services and key management SWS_CryptoDriver p. 24.

The central execution unit is the Crypto Driver Object. It represents an independent crypto entity, such as an AES accelerator on an HSM or a software implementation for RSA. Each Crypto Driver Object is the endpoint of a crypto channel SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15. An object always processes only one job at a time. A driver with n objects can process n jobs in parallel, with jobs in the queue not counting as "in processing" (citation from version R25-11) SWS_CryptoDriver p. 23. Therefore, Crypto_ProcessJob and Crypto_CancelJob address the object via objectId [SWS_Crypto_91003] [SWS_Crypto_00122].

Context diagram: The Crypto Driver serves the CryIf via Crypto Driver Objects and uses NvM, DET, and SchM as neighboring modules. Sources: SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15, AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 28, [SWS_Crypto_91017], [SWS_Crypto_91012]

Startup, Instantiation, and Partitioning

Crypto_Init is synchronous and non-reentrant and initializes the driver [SWS_Crypto_91000]. The parameter configPtr must always be a null pointer [SWS_Crypto_00215]. Interpretation: The configuration is therefore not selected at runtime, but is likely bound statically in the driver. This is consistent with the content of Crypto_ConfigType being implementation-specific [SWS_Crypto_91016]. During startup, the driver reads back persistent key values SWS_CryptoDriver p. 35. If a value cannot be loaded, it sets the affected key to invalid [SWS_Crypto_00198]. In case of a null pointer, Crypto_GetVersionInfo reports CRYPTO_E_PARAM_POINTER to the DET [SWS_Crypto_91001] SWS_CryptoDriver p. 56.

If multiple driver instances exist in an ECU, file names, API names, and published parameters must differ according to the scheme Crypto_<vi>_<ai> SWS_CryptoDriver p. 23. The NvM callbacks also carry this prefix, such as Crypto_<vi>_<ai>_NvBlock_Init_<NvBlock> [SWS_Crypto_91023]. If the driver requires random numbers internally, for instance for Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal, Crypto Driver Object 0 must be configured for this purpose [SWS_Crypto_00224]. Objects without their own default random number generator obtain their random numbers from Object 0 [SWS_Crypto_00225]. In doing so, they only call generators of their own driver [SWS_Crypto_00226].

In case of partitioning, the driver operates as an independent instance in each partition. An API call only affects the partition in which it occurs [SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00001]. The partitions of a Crypto Driver Object must be a subset of the driver partitions [SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00002]. An object for an HSM shall be assigned to at most one partition [SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00003]. The BSW Distribution Guide justifies this distribution with load balancing per crypto instance BSWDistributionGuide p. 59.

Job Processing via Crypto_ProcessJob

All crypto services run via the reentrant function Crypto_ProcessJob(objectId, job). Whether a job runs synchronously or asynchronously depends on its configuration [SWS_Crypto_91003]. This information is contained in the Crypto_JobType SWS_CryptoDriver p. 26. The driver imports the job types from Crypto_GeneralTypes.h of the CSM [SWS_Crypto_00042].

In the asynchronous case, the interface function passes only the necessary information to the primitive. The calculation can be triggered by the Main Function. After completion, the driver notifies the CryIf via CRYIF_CallbackNotification and passes the job and result SWS_CryptoDriver p. 27. Crypto_MainFunction is called cyclically when asynchronous processing is configured and job queues exist [SWS_Crypto_91012].

Sequence diagram: An asynchronous job returns immediately, is computed in the Main Function, and is completed via callback. The forwarding from the CryIf to the CSM is marked as an interpretation. Sources: [SWS_Crypto_91003], [SWS_Crypto_91012], SWS_CryptoDriver p. 27

The job contains a flag field with the operation modes START, UPDATE, and FINISH. The flags can be combined and are then always executed in this order. START cancels all previous requests of the same job SWS_CryptoDriver p. 25. A single call corresponds to the combination START|UPDATE|FINISH SWS_CryptoInterface p. 22. For key management jobs, the specification recommends CRYPTO_OPERATIONMODE_SINGLECALL SWS_CryptoDriver p. 66.

Activity diagram: The flags START, UPDATE, and FINISH are evaluated in a fixed order. Sources: SWS_CryptoDriver p. 25, SWS_CryptoInterface p. 22

If job->jobRedirectionInfoRef is set and the associated configuration bit is active, the driver uses key elements instead of buffers as input or output [SWS_Crypto_00203] [SWS_Crypto_00204]. Minimum permissions apply for this: For example, an input element requires CRYPTO_RA_INTERNAL_COPY "or lower" [SWS_Crypto_00221]. On the CSM side, this corresponds to the configuration container CsmInOutRedirections AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 167.

Keys, Key Elements, and Access Rights

A key consists of one or more key elements. Examples are the key material, an initialization vector, or a seed state. Each element carries read and write rights as enumeration values whose numerical values form a hierarchy SWS_CryptoDriver p. 28. These rights must be observed during direct read and write access [SWS_Crypto_00219]. Interpretation: The requirements to execute "this operation" only in case of CRYPTO_RA_ALLOWED/CRYPTO_RA_ENCRYPTED [SWS_Crypto_00222] or CRYPTO_WA_ALLOWED/CRYPTO_WA_ENCRYPTED [SWS_Crypto_00223] presumably refer to Crypto_KeyElementGet [SWS_Crypto_91006] and Crypto_KeyElementSet [SWS_Crypto_91004]. Jobs, on the other hand, use their assigned elements without permission checks. Redirection is excluded [SWS_Crypto_00221].

Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet lists the existing element IDs of a key. Upon call, keyElementIdsLengthPtr contains the buffer size, and after completion, the actual count [SWS_Crypto_00160] SWS_CryptoDriver p. 78. Two functions are available for copying:

  • Crypto_KeyCopy copies a key with all elements within the same driver [SWS_Crypto_00155].
  • Crypto_KeyElementCopy copies a single element [SWS_Crypto_00148].

The source element must have at least the same rights as the destination. A source key requires at least CRYPTO_RA_INTERNAL_COPY [SWS_Crypto_00220]. If elements are mapped directly to flash, the synchronous call can take significantly longer SWS_CryptoDriver p. 77.

Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial copies an excerpt with source and target offset [SWS_Crypto_91015]. The function returns CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH if the source element is shorter than offset plus length [SWS_Crypto_00207] or if the maximum buffer of the target is insufficient [SWS_Crypto_00208]. Otherwise, it copies [SWS_Crypto_00209] and adjusts the target length if necessary [SWS_Crypto_00210] [SWS_Crypto_00211].

Activity diagram: Length checks and length adjustment during partial copying. Both size checks lead to the same return value, so their order is irrelevant. Sources: [SWS_Crypto_00207], [SWS_Crypto_00208], [SWS_Crypto_00209], [SWS_Crypto_00210], [SWS_Crypto_00211]

The following functions are available for the generation and derivation of key material:

  • Crypto_KeyGenerate generates new key material [SWS_Crypto_91007].
  • Crypto_KeyDerive derives a key into targetCryptoKeyId [SWS_Crypto_91008].
  • Crypto_RandomSeed feeds the seed [SWS_Crypto_91013].
  • Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal calculates its own public value for key exchange [SWS_Crypto_91009].
  • Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret stores the shared secret as an element of the same key [SWS_Crypto_91010] SWS_CryptoDriver p. 84.

Asymmetric key material is passed in standardized formats. The actual extraction of the elements is then handled by the driver SWS_CryptoDriver p. 28:

Key typeFormat according to R20-11Reference
Asymmetric with identifierRFC5958/ASN.1, CRYPTO_KE_FORMAT_BIN_IDENT_PRIVATEKEY_PKCS8[SWS_Crypto_00184]
RSARFC 8017, OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1[SWS_Crypto_00185] [SWS_Crypto_00186] [SWS_Crypto_00187] [SWS_Crypto_00188]
ECC (NIST, Brainpool)CRYPTO_KE_FORMAT_BIN_OCTET; public X|Y, private X|Y|Scalar, little endian[SWS_Crypto_00189] [SWS_Crypto_00190] [SWS_Crypto_00191]
ED25519public X, private seed K|X, little endian[SWS_Crypto_00192] [SWS_Crypto_00193]

Key State and Persistence in NvM

Each key is either valid or invalid:

  • Crypto_KeySetValid sets it to valid [SWS_Crypto_91014].
  • Crypto_KeySetInvalid sets it to invalid [SWS_Crypto_91020].
  • Crypto_KeyGetStatus returns the current state [SWS_Crypto_91019].

According to the change history, the functions for querying and invalidating the key state were added with R20-11 SWS_CryptoDriver p. 2. If a key is invalid, services such as Crypto_KeyGenerate or Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret return the value CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID SWS_CryptoDriver p. 80 SWS_CryptoDriver p. 84.

State diagram: Transitions between valid and invalid as well as invalidation during startup. The initial state after successful loading is not specified in the references and is therefore not shown. Sources: [SWS_Crypto_91014], [SWS_Crypto_91020], [SWS_Crypto_91019], [SWS_Crypto_00198]

The handling of key elements in the NvM is also new in R20-11 SWS_CryptoDriver p. 2. A key references at most one NvM block, and its KeyType comprises one or more KeyElements AUTOSAR_SWS_CryptoDriver p. 32. The driver writes the elements during validation and reads them during initialization SWS_CryptoDriver p. 35. Version R25-11 clarifies that only KEYSETVALID triggers storage, but not Crypto_KeyElementSet. This allows the driver to verify interdependent elements together and save them in a single write operation SWS_CryptoDriver p. 37.

The driver provides four callbacks for data exchange with the NvM:

  • Init initializes the block [SWS_Crypto_91023].
  • ReadFrom copies from the NvM mirror into the internal buffer [SWS_Crypto_91024].
  • WriteTo fills the mirror shortly before writing [SWS_Crypto_91025].
  • Callback reports the end of an asynchronous single block request [SWS_Crypto_91026].

Optionally, the driver uses NvM_SetRamBlockStatus and NvM_WriteBlock [SWS_Crypto_91017].

Sequence diagram: Key persistence during startup and during validation. Which NvM function triggers the write job is marked as an interpretation. Sources: [SWS_Crypto_91024], [SWS_Crypto_91025], [SWS_Crypto_91026], [SWS_Crypto_91017], SWS_CryptoDriver p. 37

Cancellation of Running Jobs

Crypto_CancelJob(objectId, job) is synchronous and reentrant, though not for the same Crypto Driver Object [SWS_Crypto_00122]. The return value depends on the processing state:

  • If the driver is currently not processing the job, it returns E_OK without further processing [SWS_Crypto_00214].
  • If it can cancel a running job, it removes it and returns E_OK [SWS_Crypto_00122].
  • If it cannot cancel it, for example due to hardware limitations, it returns CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED [SWS_Crypto_00183].

"In processing" means here that the object is actively busy with the job. A job for which only FINISH is pending is not considered as in processing SWS_CryptoDriver p. 25. To CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED, the CSM reacts with a cancellation at the next suitable step and reports it via a negative closing callback SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 80.

Activity diagram: The three outcomes of a cancellation request. Sources: [SWS_Crypto_00122], [SWS_Crypto_00183], [SWS_Crypto_00214], SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 80

Behavior in the event of an error

If development error detection is active, the driver reports the following codes to the DET: CRYPTO_E_UNINIT (0x00), CRYPTO_E_INIT_FAILED (0x01), CRYPTO_E_PARAM_POINTER (0x02), CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE (0x04), CRYPTO_E_PARAM_VALUE (0x05), as well as a code for buffers that are too small [SWS_Crypto_00040]. These codes are not returned via the API SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15. An example is Crypto_KeySetValid: Without initialization, it reports CRYPTO_E_UNINIT and returns E_NOT_OK [SWS_Crypto_00196]. In case of an invalid cryptoKeyId, it reports CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE [SWS_Crypto_00197]. The same pattern applies, for instance, to Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial [SWS_Crypto_00205] and to targetCryptoKeyId in case of Crypto_KeyDerive [SWS_Crypto_00180].

Before each job, the driver checks job->cryptoKeyId and, if applicable, targetCryptoKeyId [SWS_Crypto_00217]. For CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE, the destination must always lie within the valid range [SWS_Crypto_00202]. If a buffer is too small, the driver does not execute the operation. With DET active, it reports CRYPTO_E_SMALL_BUFFER; without DET, it returns E_NOT_OK [SWS_Crypto_00195]. For CRYPTO_HASH and CRYPTO_MACGENERATE, a result truncated to the most significant bits is output instead [SWS_Crypto_00065]. The newer document reference additionally mentions CRYPTO_RANDOMGENERATE. This is not substantiated by the present R20-11 requirements SWS_CryptoDriver p. 49.

The driver reports runtime results via return values such as CRYPTO_E_BUSY, CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL, CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL, CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE, and CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID [SWS_Crypto_91018]. When entropy is exhausted, the random service returns CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED. Crypto_ProcessJob then additionally reports the runtime error CRYPTO_E_RE_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED [SWS_Crypto_00141]. For NvM errors, there is CRYPTO_E_RE_NVM_ACCESS_FAILED [SWS_Crypto_00194]. However, the application must handle defective NvM blocks SWS_CryptoDriver p. 35.

Activity diagram: Typical check chain of a driver call from the DET checks to execution. The sequence of checks is an interpretation. Sources: [SWS_Crypto_00196], [SWS_Crypto_00197], [SWS_Crypto_00217], [SWS_Crypto_00195], [SWS_Crypto_00065], [SWS_Crypto_91018]

function Crypto_ProcessJob [SWS_Crypto_91003] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_ProcessJob (uint32 objectId, Crypto_JobType* job);

Service Crypto_ProcessJob.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d012bfb1bbb0 Provenance

The function Crypto_ProcessJob ([SWS_Crypto_91003]) serves to perform the cryptographic primitive configured in parameter job on the Crypto Driver Object referenced via objectId. The interface is reentrant. The execution behavior is synchronous or asynchronous depending on the job configuration. Via the in-out parameter job (type Crypto_JobType*), both controlling parameter structures and pointers to the result data buffers are passed.

Error Handling and Validation

Prior to job execution, the crypto driver checks the validity of the key references:

  • If job->cryptoKeyId or optionally job->targetCryptoKeyId are out of range, Crypto_ProcessJob reports the error CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE to the DET and returns E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Crypto_00217]). This also applies in particular if an invalid targetCryptoKeyId is passed for the service CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE ([SWS_Crypto_00202]).
  • If the random number generator service is requested and entropy is exhausted, the function reports the runtime error CRYPTO_E_RE_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED and returns CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED ([SWS_Crypto_00141]).
  • According to [SWS_Crypto_91003], the function acknowledges successful requests with E_OK. In the event of overload or a full queue, CRYPTO_E_BUSY is reported. Additional type-specific error codes include key access and consistency errors (CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID, CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH, CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL, CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL, CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE, CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY) as well as CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED for canceled synchronous jobs.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.

function Crypto_CancelJob [SWS_Crypto_00122] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_CancelJob (uint32 objectId, Crypto_JobType* job);

This interface removes the provided job from the queue and cancels the processing of the job if possible.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 590358fa103d Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous function Crypto_CancelJob ([SWS_Crypto_00122]) removes a passed job from the queue and cancels its processing if possible. The interface is declared via the header Crypto.h.

The input parameters include:

  • objectId (in): Identifier of the Crypto Driver Object.
  • job (inout): Pointer to the configuration of the job, which contains structures with job- and primitive-relevant information.

Return values and behavior

The function signals the result via the following return values of type Std_ReturnType:

  • E_OK: The request was successful and the job was removed from the queue ([SWS_Crypto_00122]). If the Crypto Driver detects no errors and is not processing the job at the time of the call at all, E_OK is likewise returned without further processing ([SWS_Crypto_00214]).
  • CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED: If the driver detects no errors but cannot cancel the job (e.g. due to hardware restrictions), this status is reported ([SWS_Crypto_00183]). The job is considered canceled, but continues to be executed; no results are transmitted to the application ([SWS_Crypto_00122]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed and the job could not be removed ([SWS_Crypto_00122]).

Concurrency and Limitations

Crypto_CancelJob is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same Crypto Driver Object (objectId) ([SWS_Crypto_00122]).

function Crypto_KeyElementSet [SWS_Crypto_91004] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyElementSet (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32 key ElementId, const uint8* keyPtr, uint32 key Length);

Sets the given key element bytes to the key identified by crypto Key Id.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 0e26169c2384 Provenance

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyElementSet serves to set the raw data of a key element for a key identified via cryptoKeyId in the Crypto Driver ([SWS_Crypto_91004]). It is declared in the header file Crypto.h and has the service ID 0x04 ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).

Usage and Parameters

When called, the key (cryptoKeyId), the respective key element (keyElementId), a pointer to the source buffer (keyPtr), and the length of the bytes to be written (keyLength) must be passed ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).

Error Handling and Return Values

The function returns the execution status via Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Crypto_91004]):

  • E_OK: The request was successful ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed generally ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The Crypto Driver Object is currently busy ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: Write access was denied ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key element of the key is not available ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: The size of the key element does not match the buffer length of the passed data ([SWS_Crypto_91004]).

Concurrency

The interface is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Crypto_91004]). Concurrent calls must therefore be synchronized on the caller side.

function Crypto_KeySetValid [SWS_Crypto_91014] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeySetValid (uint32 crypto KeyId);

Sets the key state of the key identified by crypto Key Id to valid.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b973bc4c5836 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The function Crypto_KeySetValid ([SWS_Crypto_91014]) sets the state of the key referenced via the identifier cryptoKeyId to valid (valid).\n It is provided via the header file Crypto.h and has the service ID 0x05.\n Execution of the function is synchronous. As an input parameter, it expects cryptoKeyId of type uint32, which contains the identifier of the key to be validated.

Error Handling and Return Values

The return value of type Std_ReturnType signals the result of the operation ([SWS_Crypto_91014]):

  • E_OK: The request was successful and the state of the key was set to valid.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the affected crypto driver object (Crypto Driver Object) is currently busy.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_Crypto_91014], Crypto_KeySetValid is defined as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant).\n Callers must ensure that concurrent accesses are avoided or coordinated. In addition, calling code must take the potential result CRYPTO_E_BUSY into account and react accordingly if the driver object is still occupied with other tasks at the time of the call.

This usage note is based on the specifications of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

use

The function Crypto_KeySetInvalid ([SWS_Crypto_91020]) serves to set the status of the passed key to invalid. The function operates synchronously and is available via the header Crypto.h with the service ID 0x15.

Parameters of the interface:

  • cryptoKeyId (in): Passes the identifier of the key whose status is to be marked as invalid. Input/output and pure output parameters (inout/out) do not exist.

Error Handling and Return Values

The function returns a value of type Std_ReturnType as a result:

  • E_OK: The request was successful and the status was updated.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is currently busy.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to the specification, Crypto_KeySetInvalid is classified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). Callers must therefore ensure that no simultaneous or uncoordinated calls take place for the same instance or the same driver context.

Note: This usage note is based on the specification data for [SWS_Crypto_91020] from the AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

function Crypto_KeyElementGet [SWS_Crypto_91006] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyElementGet (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32 key ElementId, uint8* resultPtr, uint32* result LengthPtr);

This interface shall be used to get a key element of the key identified by the crypto

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: f85d96ee9c8a Provenance

use

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyElementGet reads a key element specified by cryptoKeyId and keyElementId and copies its data into the buffer resultPtr [SWS_Crypto_91006]. The interface is provided via the header Crypto.h [SWS_Crypto_91006].

On call, the inout parameter resultLengthPtr must contain the size of the target buffer. If the key element is configured for partial access, resultLengthPtr passes the desired read amount; upon successful completion, the pointer contains the actually stored data length [SWS_Crypto_91006].

Error Handling and Return Values

The return value of type Std_ReturnType signals the success or the specific error cause of the operation [SWS_Crypto_91006]:

  • E_OK: The request was completed successfully [SWS_Crypto_91006].
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed generally [SWS_Crypto_91006].
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the Crypto Driver Object is busy [SWS_Crypto_91006].
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key element of the key is not available [SWS_Crypto_91006].
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Read access to the key element was denied [SWS_Crypto_91006].
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The source key element is uninitialized [SWS_Crypto_91006].

Concurrency and Limitations

Crypto_KeyElementGet is specified as reentrant [SWS_Crypto_91006]. Since the call executes in a synchronous blocking manner, it should be noted that for key elements stored directly in flash memory, longer execution delays may occur [SWS_Crypto_91006].

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

function Crypto_KeyGetStatus [SWS_Crypto_91019] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyGetStatus (uint32 crypto KeyId, Crypto_Key StatusType* key StatusPtr);

Returns the key state of the key identified by crypto Key Id.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 7de5106342e7 Provenance

use

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyGetStatus serves to read out the current status of a cryptographic key ([SWS_Crypto_91019]). The key to be queried is specified via the input parameter cryptoKeyId ([SWS_Crypto_91019]). The query result is provided via the output pointer keyStatusPtr of type Crypto_KeyStatusType*, which points to the memory area where the status is to be stored ([SWS_Crypto_91019]).

The interface is available via the header file Crypto.h and has the service ID 0x14 ([SWS_Crypto_91019]). As its return value, the call delivers the type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Crypto_91019]):

  • E_OK: The request was successful and the key status was validly stored in the target memory ([SWS_Crypto_91019]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The execution of the request failed ([SWS_Crypto_91019]).

Error handling

If the key status cannot be determined, the function signals the failure immediately via the return value E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Crypto_91019]). Specific development errors (DET) or error notifications to Diagnostic Event Management (DEM) are not separately listed in the available specification data for this element.

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is classified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Crypto_91019]). In the event of parallel access from multiple tasks or different execution contexts, external synchronization by the caller is therefore likely required to prevent concurrent calls.

function Crypto_KeyElementCopy [SWS_Crypto_00148] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyElementCopy (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32 key ElementId, uint32 target Crypto KeyId, uint32 target Key ElementId);

Service Crypto_KeyElementCopy.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: a9ecee086479 Provenance

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyElementCopy ([SWS_Crypto_00148]) serves to copy a key element within the same crypto driver to a target key element. It is declared in Crypto.h and has the service ID 0x0f.

Parameters and call behavior

  • cryptoKeyId: Identifier of the key containing the source key element ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • keyElementId: Identifier of the source key element ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • targetCryptoKeyId: Identifier of the key intended to receive the target key element ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • targetKeyElementId: Identifier of the target key element ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).

Since the copy process is executed synchronously, noticeable delays can occur during the function call if the affected key element is stored directly in flash memory ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).

Error Handling and Return Values

The function returns a status of type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Crypto_00148]):

  • E_OK: Copy process successful ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • E_NOT_OK: General malfunction during execution ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The Crypto Driver Object is busy ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key element of at least one involved key is not available ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Reading or extracting the source element is not allowed ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: Writing the target element is not allowed ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: Incompatible sizes of the involved key elements ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The source key element is uninitialized ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is reentrant, but must not be called concurrently for the same cryptoKeyId ([SWS_Crypto_00148]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

function Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial [SWS_Crypto_91015] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32 key ElementId, uint32 key Element Source Offset, uint32 key Element Target Offset, uint32 key Element Copy Length, uint32 target Crypto KeyId, uint32 target Key ElementId);

Service Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: db77a8a6ba61 Provenance

use

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial ([SWS_Crypto_91015]) copies a partial range of a source key element to a target key element within the same crypto driver ([SWS_Crypto_00209]). The source and target keys are determined via cryptoKeyId and targetCryptoKeyId, and the associated key elements via keyElementId and targetKeyElementId. Via keyElementSourceOffset, keyElementTargetOffset, and keyElementCopyLength, the slice to be copied is defined byte-accurately ([SWS_Crypto_91015]). Upon successful execution, the call returns E_OK ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).

Error handling

In case of an error, the following return values and error messages are generated:

  • If the crypto driver is not yet initialized and development error detection is enabled, the function reports CRYPTO_E_UNINIT to the DET and returns E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Crypto_00205]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH is returned if the total length of the source element is smaller than keyElementSourceOffset + keyElementCopyLength ([SWS_Crypto_00207]) or the available buffer of the target element is smaller than keyElementTargetOffset + keyElementCopyLength ([SWS_Crypto_00208]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY signals that the source key element is not initialized ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE occurs if at least one requested key element is not available ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL and CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL, respectively, indicate that reading the source element or writing to the target element is not allowed ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY signals that the responsible crypto driver object is busy ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).
  • General errors lead to the return of E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryptoKeyId ([SWS_Crypto_91015]). Since the service runs synchronously, larger execution delays can occur if the affected key element is located directly in flash memory ([SWS_Crypto_91015]).

This usage note is based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I2)

function Crypto_KeyCopy [SWS_Crypto_00155] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyCopy (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32 target Crypto KeyId);

Copies a key with all its elements to another key in the same crypto driver. Note: If the actual key element is directly mapped to flash memory, there could be a bigger delay when calling this function (synchronous operation)

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: c0d942d1fca1 Provenance

use

The function Crypto_KeyCopy ([SWS_Crypto_00155]) copies a key including all associated key elements to a target key within the same crypto driver. It is executed synchronously and is available via Crypto.h under the service ID 0x10. cryptoKeyId serves as the identifier of the source key and targetCryptoKeyId as the identifier of the target key as input parameters.

Error Handling and Return Values

The return value of type Std_ReturnType signals the result of the operation:

  • E_OK: The copy operation was successful.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: At least one of the requested keys is not available.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Reading the source key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: Writing the target key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: The sizes of the key elements are not compatible with each other.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The source key element is uninitialized.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_Crypto_00155], Crypto_KeyCopy is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryptoKeyId. If the respective key element is stored directly in flash memory, a noticeable delay may occur when calling this synchronous function.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.

function Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet [SWS_Crypto_00160] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32* key Element IdsPtr, uint32* key Element Ids LengthPtr);

Used to retrieve information which key elements are available in a given key.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e37eafb3497d Provenance

Usage of Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet ([SWS_Crypto_00160], service ID 0x11) serves to retrieve information about which key element IDs are present in a specified cryptographic key. The interface is provided via the header Crypto.h.

Parameters are passed via:

  • cryptoKeyId (in): Identifier of the key whose available element IDs are to be exported.
  • keyElementIdsPtr (out): Pointer to the buffer array in which the exported key element IDs are stored.
  • keyElementIdsLengthPtr (inout): Pointer to a memory location for the buffer length. On call, this parameter must contain the size of the buffer provided by keyElementIdsPtr. After completion of the request, the actual number of available key elements is stored here.

Return Values and Error Behavior

The function reports the execution status via Std_ReturnType:

  • E_OK: The request was successful.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the relevant Crypto Driver Object is busy.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_Crypto_00160], the function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryptoKeyId. Concurrent calls with an identical key identifier are therefore not permitted.

This usage note was automatically generated based on the AUTOSAR specification for Classic Platform Release R20-11.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

function Crypto_RandomSeed [SWS_Crypto_91013] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_RandomSeed (uint32 crypto KeyId, const uint8* seedPtr, uint32 seed Length);

This function generates the internal seed state using the pro vided entropy source. Furthermore, this function can be used to update the seed state with new entropy

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 3fc244b5eb9e Provenance

The synchronous function Crypto_RandomSeed ([SWS_Crypto_91013]) serves to generate or update the internal seed state of a key using a provided entropy source.

Usage and Parameters

The interface is available via header Crypto.h and is executed synchronously. It accepts the following input parameters:

  • cryptoKeyId: Identifier of the key for which the new seed is to be generated or updated.
  • seedPtr: Pointer to the memory area containing the data to feed the seed.
  • seedLength: Length of the passed seed data in bytes.

Return Values and Error Handling

The return value of type Std_ReturnType signals the result of the operation:

  • E_OK: The request was processed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The execution failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID: The operation fails because the key identified by cryptoKeyId is in the \"invalid\" state.

Concurrency

According to [SWS_Crypto_91013], the function is implemented as reentrant, but explicitly not when using the same cryptoKeyId at the same time. Concurrent calls for the same key must be excluded on the caller side.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d6df0db77cba Provenance

The function Crypto_KeyGenerate serves to generate new key material and stores it directly in the key referenced via parameter cryptoKeyId ([SWS_Crypto_91007]). It is provided via header Crypto.h and has the service ID 0x07 ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).

Call and Semantics

  • Synchronous/Asynchronous: The call is processed synchronously ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).
  • Parameters: cryptoKeyId (input parameter of type uint32) identifies the target key to be updated with the generated value ([SWS_Crypto_91007]). Additional input or output parameters do not exist ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The function reports the execution status via the return type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Crypto_91007]):

  • E_OK: Key generation was successful ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is currently busy ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The request failed due to an uninitialized source key element ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID: The request failed because the status of the key specified by cryptoKeyId is invalid ([SWS_Crypto_91007]).

Concurrency and Limitations

Crypto_KeyGenerate is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryptoKeyId ([SWS_Crypto_91007]). Concurrent calls for identical key IDs must therefore be avoided or serialized at caller level.

This usage note was generated automatically on the basis of the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.

function Crypto_KeyDerive [SWS_Crypto_91008] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyDerive (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint32 target Crypto KeyId);

Derives a new key by using the key elements in the given key identified by the crypto Key Id. The given key contains the key elements for the password, salt. The derived key is stored in the key element with the id 1 of the key identified by target Crypto Key Id. The number of iterations is given in the key element CRYPTO_ KE_ KEYDERIVATION_ ITERATIONS.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d3a392565677 Provenance

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyDerive ([SWS_Crypto_91008]) serves to derive a new cryptographic key. Here, key elements for password and salt from the source key referenced by cryptoKeyId as well as the number of iterations from key element CRYPTO_KE_KEYDERIVATION_ITERATIONS are used. The derived key is stored in the key element with ID 1 of the target key targetCryptoKeyId.

Call and Parameters

  • cryptoKeyId: Identifier of the source key that provides the required parameters for key derivation.
  • targetCryptoKeyId: Identifier of the target key in which the derived key is stored.

Return Values and Error Handling

  • E_OK: The key derivation was performed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed. If parameter targetCryptoKeyId is outside the valid range of values and development error detection is enabled for the crypto driver, the function reports CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE to the DET and returns E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Crypto_00180]).
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: At least one required key element of the source key is not initialized.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID: The status of the source key cryptoKeyId is invalid.

Concurrency

According to [SWS_Crypto_91008], the function is designed to be reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryptoKeyId. Concurrent calls with the same source key must therefore be avoided on the caller side.

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR Classic R20-11 specification.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal (uint32 crypto KeyId, uint8* public ValuePtr, uint32* public Value LengthPtr);

Calculates the public value for the key exchange a nd stores the public key in the memory location pointed by the public value pointer.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b3e9d0d3dfa4 Provenance

use

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal ([SWS_Crypto_91009]) computes the public key value for a key exchange protocol based on the key identified via cryptoKeyId and stores it in the target memory area publicValuePtr.\nPrior to the call, the provided buffer size must be passed via the input/output parameter publicValueLengthPtr; after completion of execution, this pointer contains the actual length of the generated value. The function is provided via Crypto.h.

Return Values and Error Handling

The status of execution is signaled via the return type Std_ReturnType:

  • E_OK: The request was executed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The execution failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The required Crypto Driver Object is currently busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The source key element is not initialized.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID: The key status of the key specified via cryptoKeyId is invalid (invalid).

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is implemented as reentrant, but must not be called concurrently for the same cryptoKeyId ([SWS_Crypto_91009]).

Interaction

If the crypto driver requires a random number generator (RNG) for internal operations such as Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal, the first Crypto Driver Object (object number 0) is to be configured for this purpose according to [SWS_Crypto_00224].

function Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret [SWS_Crypto_91010] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret (uint32 crypto KeyId, const uint8* partner Public ValuePtr, uint32 partner Public Value Length);

Calculates the shared secret key for the key exchange with the key material of the key identified by the crypto Key Id and the partner public key. The shared secret key is stored as a key element in the same key.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: a1a4c6c662fc Provenance

use

The synchronous function Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret calculates the shared secret (Shared Secret Key) for a key exchange protocol according to [SWS_Crypto_91010]. The calculation is performed on the basis of the key material of the key identified via cryptoKeyId and the public value of the partner. The resulting secret is stored as a key element directly in the same key.

The function expects the following input parameters ([SWS_Crypto_91010]):

  • cryptoKeyId: Identifier of the key to be used for the key exchange protocol.
  • partnerPublicValuePtr: Pointer to the memory area containing the public value of the partner.
  • partnerPublicValueLength: Length of the partner's public value in bytes.

Error Handling and Return Values

The function call returns a status of type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Crypto_91010]):

  • E_OK: The calculation and storage of the shared secret was successful.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The request failed because a required source key element is not initialized.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID: The request failed because the passed key is in the \"invalid\" state.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_Crypto_91010], the function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryptoKeyId. Concurrent calls with an identical key ID must therefore be synchronized or avoided on caller side. The service is available via the header Crypto.h with the service ID 0x0a.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="590358fa103d5033e984f073fe4e406d98ff8c4cd9ec648fc29fc8aae0c4b6c1" data-trace-output="e05de9181a0465623dc14829f0a8a6a8b8ad792d2da18d256a3564d347ffb5fa" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous function <code>Crypto_CancelJob</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>) removes a passed job from the queue and cancels its processing if possible. The interface is declared via the header <code>Crypto.h</code>.
  </p>
  <p>
    The input parameters include:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>objectId</code> (in): Identifier of the Crypto Driver Object.</li>
    <li><code>job</code> (inout): Pointer to the configuration of the job, which contains structures with job- and primitive-relevant information.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Return values and behavior</h4>
  <p>
    The function signals the result via the following return values of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful and the job was removed from the queue (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>). If the Crypto Driver detects no errors and is not processing the job at the time of the call at all, <code>E_OK</code> is likewise returned without further processing (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00214" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00214">[SWS_Crypto_00214]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED</code>: If the driver detects no errors but cannot cancel the job (e.g. due to hardware restrictions), this status is reported (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00183" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00183">[SWS_Crypto_00183]</a>). The job is considered canceled, but continues to be executed; no results are transmitted to the application (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed and the job could not be removed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>).</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    <code>Crypto_CancelJob</code> is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same Crypto Driver Object (<code>objectId</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>).
  </p>
  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was created automatically based on the specification.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="a9ecee086479fb371180e93674b8213418de302bdcbb2b77b89b7099f77e175b" data-trace-output="2a8f2da4b9349055580541b9cef3bd5fe78cdc10664cf7c84796aee80ea41236" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyElementCopy</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>) serves to copy a key element within the same crypto driver to a target key element. It is declared in <code>Crypto.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x0f</code>.</p>

  <h4>Parameters and call behavior</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryptoKeyId</code>: Identifier of the key containing the source key element (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>keyElementId</code>: Identifier of the source key element (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>targetCryptoKeyId</code>: Identifier of the key intended to receive the target key element (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>targetKeyElementId</code>: Identifier of the target key element (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Since the copy process is executed synchronously, noticeable delays can occur during the function call if the affected key element is stored directly in flash memory (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The function returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: Copy process successful (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: General malfunction during execution (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The Crypto Driver Object is busy (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The requested key element of at least one involved key is not available (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>: Reading or extracting the source element is not allowed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>: Writing the target element is not allowed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: Incompatible sizes of the involved key elements (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The source key element is uninitialized (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is reentrant, but must not be called concurrently for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The function <code>Crypto_KeyCopy</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00155" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00155">[SWS_Crypto_00155]</a>) copies a key including all associated key elements to a target key within the same crypto driver. It is executed synchronously and is available via <code>Crypto.h</code> under the service ID <code>0x10</code>. <code>cryptoKeyId</code> serves as the identifier of the source key and <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code> as the identifier of the target key as input parameters.</p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> signals the result of the operation:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The copy operation was successful.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: At least one of the requested keys is not available.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>: Reading the source key element is not allowed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>: Writing the target key element is not allowed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The sizes of the key elements are not compatible with each other.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The source key element is uninitialized.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00155" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00155">[SWS_Crypto_00155]</a>, <code>Crypto_KeyCopy</code> is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code>. If the respective key element is stored directly in flash memory, a noticeable delay may occur when calling this synchronous function.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>
</div>

  </p>
  <p>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Behavior</h4>
  <p>

  </p>

    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the relevant Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00160" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00160">[SWS_Crypto_00160]</a>, the function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code>. <div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="d012bfb1bbb05e08d1f8f364013c27bc928611d20c5b3acb2eb9363e1d56b929" data-trace-output="a9bfb52101975c9d443ab28e1336f39bbe3831ecb288cf99ab568464cf7fc268" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>
    The function <code>Crypto_ProcessJob</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91003">[SWS_Crypto_91003]</a>) serves to perform the cryptographic primitive configured in parameter <code>job</code> on the Crypto Driver Object referenced via <code>objectId</code>. The interface is reentrant. The execution behavior is synchronous or asynchronous depending on the job configuration. Via the in-out parameter <code>job</code> (type <code>Crypto_JobType*</code>), both controlling parameter structures and pointers to the result data buffers are passed.
  </p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Validation</h4>
  <p>
    Prior to job execution, the crypto driver checks the validity of the key references:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      If <code>job-&gt;cryptoKeyId</code> or optionally <code>job-&gt;targetCryptoKeyId</code> are out of range, <code>Crypto_ProcessJob</code> reports the error <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> to the DET and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00217" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00217">[SWS_Crypto_00217]</a>). This also applies in particular if an invalid <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code> is passed for the service <code>CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00202" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00202">[SWS_Crypto_00202]</a>).
    </li>
    <li>
      If the random number generator service is requested and entropy is exhausted, the function reports the runtime error <code>CRYPTO_E_RE_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED</code> and returns <code>CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00141" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00141">[SWS_Crypto_00141]</a>).
    </li>
    <li>

  <p>

It is declared in the header file <code>Crypto.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x04</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).
  </p>
  <h4>Usage and Parameters</h4>
  <p>
    When called, the key (<code>cryptoKeyId</code>), the respective key element (<code>keyElementId</code>), a pointer to the source buffer (<code>keyPtr</code>), and the length of the bytes to be written (<code>keyLength</code>) must be passed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).
  </p>
  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The function returns the execution status via <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed generally (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The Crypto Driver Object is currently busy (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>: Write access was denied (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The requested key element of the key is not available (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The size of the key element does not match the buffer length of the passed data (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>).</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency</h4>
  <p>
    The interface is specified as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>). Concurrent calls must therefore be synchronized on the caller side.

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyElementGet</code> reads a key element specified by <code>cryptoKeyId</code> and <code>keyElementId</code> and copies its data into the buffer <code>resultPtr</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>. The interface is provided via the header <code>Crypto.h</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</p>
  <p>On call, the inout parameter <code>resultLengthPtr</code> must contain the size of the target buffer. If the key element is configured for partial access, <code>resultLengthPtr</code> passes the desired read amount; upon successful completion, the pointer contains the actually stored data length <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</p>
  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> signals the success or the specific error cause of the operation <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was completed successfully <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed generally <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the Crypto Driver Object is busy <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The requested key element of the key is not available <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>: Read access to the key element was denied <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The source key element is uninitialized <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p><code>Crypto_KeyElementGet</code> is specified as reentrant <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>. Since the call executes in a synchronous blocking manner, it should be noted that for key elements stored directly in flash memory, longer execution delays may occur <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a>.</p>

  <p>The function <code>Crypto_KeyGenerate</code> serves to generate new key material and stores it directly in the key referenced via parameter <code>cryptoKeyId</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>). It is provided via header <code>Crypto.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x07</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Call and Semantics</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Synchronous/Asynchronous:</strong> The call is processed synchronously (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
    <li><strong>Parameters:</strong> <code>cryptoKeyId</code> (input parameter of type <code>uint32</code>) identifies the target key to be updated with the generated value (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>). Additional input or output parameters do not exist (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The function reports the execution status via the return type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: Key generation was successful (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is currently busy (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The request failed due to an uninitialized source key element (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The request failed because the status of the key specified by <code>cryptoKeyId</code> is invalid (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p><code>Crypto_KeyGenerate</code> is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>).   <p>The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyDerive</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91008">[SWS_Crypto_91008]</a>) serves to derive a new cryptographic key. Here, key elements for password and salt from the source key referenced by <code>cryptoKeyId</code> as well as the number of iterations from key element <code>CRYPTO_KE_KEYDERIVATION_ITERATIONS</code> are used. The derived key is stored in the key element with ID 1 of the target key <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code>.</p>

  <h4>Call and Parameters</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryptoKeyId</code>: Identifier of the source key that provides the required parameters for key derivation.</li>
    <li><code>targetCryptoKeyId</code>: Identifier of the target key in which the derived key is stored.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The key derivation was performed successfully.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed. If parameter <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code> is outside the valid range of values and development error detection is enabled for the crypto driver, the function reports <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> to the DET and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00180" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00180">[SWS_Crypto_00180]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: At least one required key element of the source key is not initialized.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The status of the source key <code>cryptoKeyId</code> is invalid.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91008">[SWS_Crypto_91008]</a>, the function is designed to be reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code>. Concurrent calls with the same source key must therefore be avoided on the caller side.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR Classic R20-11 specification.</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>
The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91009">[SWS_Crypto_91009]</a>) computes the public key value for a key exchange protocol based on the key identified via <code>cryptoKeyId</code> and stores it in the target memory area <code>publicValuePtr</code>.\nPrior to the call, the provided buffer size must be passed via the input/output parameter <code>publicValueLengthPtr</code>; after completion of execution, this pointer contains the actual length of the generated value. The function is provided via <code>Crypto.h</code>.
</p>

<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>
The status of execution is signaled via the return type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>:
</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was executed successfully.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The execution failed.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The required Crypto Driver Object is currently busy.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The source key element is not initialized.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The key status of the key specified via <code>cryptoKeyId</code> is invalid (<code>invalid</code>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>
The function is implemented as reentrant, but must not be called concurrently for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91009">[SWS_Crypto_91009]</a>).
</p>

<h4>Interaction</h4>
<p>
If the crypto driver requires a random number generator (RNG) for internal operations such as <code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal</code>, the first Crypto Driver Object (object number 0) is to be configured for this purpose according to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00224" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00224">[SWS_Crypto_00224]</a>.
</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret</code> calculates the shared secret (Shared Secret Key) for a key exchange protocol according to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91010">[SWS_Crypto_91010]</a>. The calculation is performed on the basis of the key material of the key identified via <code>cryptoKeyId</code> and the public value of the partner. The resulting secret is stored as a key element directly in the same key.
  </p>
  <p>
    The function expects the following input parameters (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91010">[SWS_Crypto_91010]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryptoKeyId</code>: Identifier of the key to be used for the key exchange protocol.</li>
    <li><code>partnerPublicValuePtr</code>: Pointer to the memory area containing the public value of the partner.</li>
    <li><code>partnerPublicValueLength</code>: Length of the partner's public value in bytes.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The function call returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91010">[SWS_Crypto_91010]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The calculation and storage of the shared secret was successful.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The request failed because a required source key element is not initialized.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The request failed because the passed key is in the \"invalid\" state.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91010">[SWS_Crypto_91010]</a>, the function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code>. Concurrent calls with an identical key ID must therefore be synchronized or avoided on caller side. The service is available via the header <code>Crypto.h</code> with the service ID <code>0x0a</code>.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.</p>

  <p>The synchronous function <code>Crypto_RandomSeed</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91013">[SWS_Crypto_91013]</a>) serves to generate or update the internal seed state of a key using a provided entropy source.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Parameters</h4>
  <p>The interface is available via header <code>Crypto.h</code> and is executed synchronously. It accepts the following input parameters:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryptoKeyId</code>: Identifier of the key for which the new seed is to be generated or updated.</li>
    <li><code>seedPtr</code>: Pointer to the memory area containing the data to feed the seed.</li>
    <li><code>seedLength</code>: Length of the passed seed data in bytes.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> signals the result of the operation:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was processed successfully.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The execution failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The operation fails because the key identified by <code>cryptoKeyId</code> is in the \"invalid\" state.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91013">[SWS_Crypto_91013]</a>, the function is implemented as reentrant, but explicitly not when using the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code> at the same time. Concurrent calls for the same key must be excluded on the caller side.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>Crypto_KeySetValid</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91014">[SWS_Crypto_91014]</a>) sets the state of the key referenced via the identifier <code>cryptoKeyId</code> to valid (<em>valid</em>).\n    It is provided via the header file <code>Crypto.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x05</code>.\n    Execution of the function is synchronous. As an input parameter, it expects <code>cryptoKeyId</code> of type <code>uint32</code>, which contains the identifier of the key to be validated.
  </p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> signals the result of the operation (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91014">[SWS_Crypto_91014]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful and the state of the key was set to valid.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the affected crypto driver object (<em>Crypto Driver Object</em>) is currently busy.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91014">[SWS_Crypto_91014]</a>, <code>Crypto_KeySetValid</code> is defined as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>).\n    Callers must ensure that concurrent accesses are avoided or coordinated. In addition, calling code must take the potential result <code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code> into account and react accordingly if the driver object is still occupied with other tasks at the time of the call.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">
    This usage note is based on the specifications of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.
  </p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="db77a8a6ba618be5de4cbe9348e15ff24766b9391a49a9a454e8b731471d4d81" data-trace-output="6db429ad2dcff14ae0b393c4c04cd577cf26a1054ca457f3dd77ac9c4c285e9d" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>) copies a partial range of a source key element to a target key element within the same crypto driver (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00209" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00209">[SWS_Crypto_00209]</a>). The source and target keys are determined via <code>cryptoKeyId</code> and <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code>, and the associated key elements via <code>keyElementId</code> and <code>targetKeyElementId</code>. Via <code>keyElementSourceOffset</code>, <code>keyElementTargetOffset</code>, and <code>keyElementCopyLength</code>, the slice to be copied is defined byte-accurately (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>). Upon successful execution, the call returns <code>E_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</p>

<h4>Error handling</h4>
<p>In case of an error, the following return values and error messages are generated:</p>
<ul>
<li>If the crypto driver is not yet initialized and development error detection is enabled, the function reports <code>CRYPTO_E_UNINIT</code> to the DET and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00205" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00205">[SWS_Crypto_00205]</a>).</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code> is returned if the total length of the source element is smaller than <code>keyElementSourceOffset + keyElementCopyLength</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00207" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00207">[SWS_Crypto_00207]</a>) or the available buffer of the target element is smaller than <code>keyElementTargetOffset + keyElementCopyLength</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00208" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00208">[SWS_Crypto_00208]</a>).</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code> signals that the source key element is not initialized (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code> occurs if at least one requested key element is not available (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code> and <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>, respectively, indicate that reading the source element or writing to the target element is not allowed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code> signals that the responsible crypto driver object is busy (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</li>
<li>General errors lead to the return of <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>The function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryptoKeyId</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>). Since the service runs synchronously, larger execution delays can occur if the affected key element is located directly in flash memory (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>).</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>Crypto_KeyGetStatus</code> serves to read out the current status of a cryptographic key (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>).
