  <p>The interface is available via the header file <code>Crypto.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x14</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>). As its return value, the call delivers the type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful and the key status was validly stored in the target memory (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The execution of the request failed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>If the key status cannot be determined, the function signals the failure immediately via the return value <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>). Specific development errors (DET) or error notifications to Diagnostic Event Management (DEM) are not separately listed in the available specification data for this element.</p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is classified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>). In the event of parallel access from multiple tasks or different execution contexts, external synchronization by the caller is therefore likely required to prevent concurrent calls.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification for <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>.</p>
  <!-- annahmen: 1) Bei parallelen Aufrufen dürfte eine externe Synchronisation durch den Aufrufer erforderlich sein – Begründung: SWS_Crypto_91019 stuft die Funktion als Non Reentrant ein, spezifiziert jedoch keine internen Synchronisationsmechanismen. -->
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="4e5a0a5e361f5fce190100216cf49a06687dab3c315e8f36a9b3f3d20e727533" data-trace-output="6a493d9cd769e375918ebc2f74364d93077b583ea1eb40a1b278897c2c20cb4a" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>Crypto_KeySetInvalid</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91020">[SWS_Crypto_91020]</a>) serves to set the status of the passed key to invalid. The function operates synchronously and is available via the header <code>Crypto.h</code> with the service ID <code>0x15</code>.
  </p>
  <p>
    Parameters of the interface:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryptoKeyId</code> (in): Passes the identifier of the key whose status is to be marked as invalid. Input/output and pure output parameters (inout/out) do not exist.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The function returns a value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> as a result:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful and the status was updated.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is currently busy.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    According to the specification, <code>Crypto_KeySetInvalid</code> is classified as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>). Callers must therefore ensure that no simultaneous or uncoordinated calls take place for the same instance or the same driver context.
  </p>
  <p class="ai-note">
    Note: This usage note is based on the specification data for <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91020">[SWS_Crypto_91020]</a> from the AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.
  </p>
</div>

<h4>Role of the Crypto Driver in the Crypto Stack</h4>
<p>The Crypto Driver is located in the Microcontroller Abstraction Layer below the Crypto Interface (CryIf) and Crypto Service Manager (CSM). It provides a generic interface for synchronous and asynchronous cryptographic primitives and handles key storage, key configuration, and key management. An ECU integrates exactly one CSM and one CryIf. However, the CryIf can address multiple Crypto Drivers <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_FIGURE_Figure_7_1_CRYPTODRIVER.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_FIGURE_Figure_7_1_CRYPTODRIVER">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15</a>. The specification summarizes the service offering into two services: crypto services and key management <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_3_Design_Notes.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_3_Design_Notes">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 24</a>.</p>
<p>The central execution unit is the <em>Crypto Driver Object</em>. It represents an independent crypto entity, such as an AES accelerator on an HSM or a software implementation for RSA. Each Crypto Driver Object is the endpoint of a crypto channel <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_FIGURE_Figure_7_1_CRYPTODRIVER.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_FIGURE_Figure_7_1_CRYPTODRIVER">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15</a>. An object always processes only one job at a time. A driver with n objects can process n jobs in parallel, with jobs in the queue not counting as "in processing" (citation from version R25-11) <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_General_Behavior.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_General_Behavior">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 23</a>. Therefore, <code>Crypto_ProcessJob</code> and <code>Crypto_CancelJob</code> address the object via <code>objectId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91003">[SWS_Crypto_91003]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>.</p>

Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_FIGURE_Figure_7_1_CRYPTODRIVER.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_FIGURE_Figure_7_1_CRYPTODRIVER">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-e923d225c23cecf7.html" data-snip="FIG-e923d225c23cecf7">AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 28</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91017" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91017">[SWS_Crypto_91017]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91012">[SWS_Crypto_91012]</a></p>

<h4>Startup, Instantiation, and Partitioning</h4>
<p><code>Crypto_Init</code> is synchronous and non-reentrant and initializes the driver <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91000" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91000">[SWS_Crypto_91000]</a>. The parameter <code>configPtr</code> must always be a null pointer <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00215" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00215">[SWS_Crypto_00215]</a>. Interpretation: The configuration is therefore not selected at runtime, but is likely bound statically in the driver. This is consistent with the content of <code>Crypto_ConfigType</code> being implementation-specific <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91016" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91016">[SWS_Crypto_91016]</a>. During startup, the driver reads back persistent key values <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_NVM_SECTION_7_2_6_Key_Storage_in_NVM.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_NVM_SECTION_7_2_6_Key_Storage_in_NVM">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 35</a>. If a value cannot be loaded, it sets the affected key to invalid <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00198" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00198">[SWS_Crypto_00198]</a>. In case of a null pointer, <code>Crypto_GetVersionInfo</code> reports <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> to the DET <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91001">[SWS_Crypto_91001]</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_1_2_Crypto_GetVersionInfo.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_1_2_Crypto_GetVersionInfo">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 56</a>.</p>
<p>If multiple driver instances exist in an ECU, file names, API names, and published parameters must differ according to the scheme <code>Crypto_&lt;vi&gt;_&lt;ai&gt;</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_General_Behavior.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_General_Behavior">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 23</a>. The NvM callbacks also carry this prefix, such as <code>Crypto_&lt;vi&gt;_&lt;ai&gt;_NvBlock_Init_&lt;NvBlock&gt;</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91023" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91023">[SWS_Crypto_91023]</a>. If the driver requires random numbers internally, for instance for <code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal</code>, Crypto Driver Object 0 must be configured for this purpose <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00224" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00224">[SWS_Crypto_00224]</a>. Objects without their own default random number generator obtain their random numbers from Object 0 <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00225" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00225">[SWS_Crypto_00225]</a>. In doing so, they only call generators of their own driver <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00226" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00226">[SWS_Crypto_00226]</a>.</p>
<p>In case of partitioning, the driver operates as an independent instance in each partition. An API call only affects the partition in which it occurs <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00001">[SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00001]</a>. The partitions of a Crypto Driver Object must be a subset of the driver partitions <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00002">[SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00002]</a>. An object for an HSM shall be assigned to at most one partition <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00003">[SWS_Crypto_CONSTR_00003]</a>. The BSW Distribution Guide justifies this distribution with load balancing per crypto instance <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_BSWDISTRIBUTIONGUIDE_SECTION_2_8_Crypto_Stack_Distribution.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_BSWDISTRIBUTIONGUIDE_SECTION_2_8_Crypto_Stack_Distribution">BSWDistributionGuide p. 59</a>.</p>

<h4>Job Processing via Crypto_ProcessJob</h4>
<p>All crypto services run via the reentrant function <code>Crypto_ProcessJob(objectId, job)</code>. Whether a job runs synchronously or asynchronously depends on its configuration <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91003">[SWS_Crypto_91003]</a>. This information is contained in the <code>Crypto_JobType</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_Functional_Requirements.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_Functional_Requirements">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 26</a>. The driver imports the job types from <code>Crypto_GeneralTypes.h</code> of the CSM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00042" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00042">[SWS_Crypto_00042]</a>.</p>
<p>In the asynchronous case, the interface function passes only the necessary information to the primitive. The calculation can be triggered by the Main Function. After completion, the driver notifies the CryIf via <code>CRYIF_CallbackNotification</code> and passes the job and result <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 27</a>. <code>Crypto_MainFunction</code> is called cyclically when asynchronous processing is configured and job queues exist <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91012">[SWS_Crypto_91012]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequence diagram: An asynchronous job returns immediately, is computed in the Main Function, and is completed via callback. The forwarding from the CryIf to the CSM is marked as an interpretation. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91003">[SWS_Crypto_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91012">[SWS_Crypto_91012]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 27</a></p>
<p>The job contains a flag field with the operation modes START, UPDATE, and FINISH. The flags can be combined and are then always executed in this order. START cancels all previous requests of the same job <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 25</a>. A single call corresponds to the combination <code>START|UPDATE|FINISH</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface">SWS_CryptoInterface p. 22</a>. For key management jobs, the specification recommends <code>CRYPTO_OPERATIONMODE_SINGLECALL</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_Key_Management_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_Key_Management_Interface">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 66</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Activity diagram: The flags START, UPDATE, and FINISH are evaluated in a fixed order. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 25</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface">SWS_CryptoInterface p. 22</a></p>
<p>If <code>job-&gt;jobRedirectionInfoRef</code> is set and the associated configuration bit is active, the driver uses key elements instead of buffers as input or output <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00203">[SWS_Crypto_00203]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00204" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00204">[SWS_Crypto_00204]</a>. Minimum permissions apply for this: For example, an input element requires <code>CRYPTO_RA_INTERNAL_COPY</code> "or lower" <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00221" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00221">[SWS_Crypto_00221]</a>. On the CSM side, this corresponds to the configuration container <code>CsmInOutRedirections</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-fe85ba6a0aac3e11.html" data-snip="FIG-fe85ba6a0aac3e11">AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 167</a>.</p>

<h4>Keys, Key Elements, and Access Rights</h4>
<p>A key consists of one or more key elements. Examples are the key material, an initialization vector, or a seed state. Each element carries read and write rights as enumeration values whose numerical values form a hierarchy <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_4_Key_Management.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_4_Key_Management">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 28</a>. These rights must be observed during direct read and write access <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00219" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00219">[SWS_Crypto_00219]</a>. Interpretation: The requirements to execute "this operation" only in case of <code>CRYPTO_RA_ALLOWED</code>/<code>CRYPTO_RA_ENCRYPTED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00222" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00222">[SWS_Crypto_00222]</a> or <code>CRYPTO_WA_ALLOWED</code>/<code>CRYPTO_WA_ENCRYPTED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00223">[SWS_Crypto_00223]</a> presumably refer to <code>Crypto_KeyElementGet</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91006">[SWS_Crypto_91006]</a> and <code>Crypto_KeyElementSet</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91004">[SWS_Crypto_91004]</a>. Jobs, on the other hand, use their assigned elements without permission checks. Redirection is excluded <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00221" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00221">[SWS_Crypto_00221]</a>.</p>
<p><code>Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet</code> lists the existing element IDs of a key. Upon call, <code>keyElementIdsLengthPtr</code> contains the buffer size, and after completion, the actual count <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00160" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00160">[SWS_Crypto_00160]</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_4_4_Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_4_4_Crypto_KeyElementIdsGet">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 78</a>. Two functions are available for copying:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyCopy</code> copies a key with all elements within the same driver <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00155" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00155">[SWS_Crypto_00155]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyElementCopy</code> copies a single element <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00148" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00148">[SWS_Crypto_00148]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>The source element must have at least the same rights as the destination. A source key requires at least <code>CRYPTO_RA_INTERNAL_COPY</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00220" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00220">[SWS_Crypto_00220]</a>. If elements are mapped directly to flash, the synchronous call can take significantly longer <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_4_3_Crypto_KeyCopy.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_4_3_Crypto_KeyCopy">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 77</a>.</p>
<p><code>Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial</code> copies an excerpt with source and target offset <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91015">[SWS_Crypto_91015]</a>. The function returns <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code> if the source element is shorter than offset plus length <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00207" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00207">[SWS_Crypto_00207]</a> or if the maximum buffer of the target is insufficient <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00208" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00208">[SWS_Crypto_00208]</a>. Otherwise, it copies <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00209" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00209">[SWS_Crypto_00209]</a> and adjusts the target length if necessary <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00210" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00210">[SWS_Crypto_00210]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00211" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00211">[SWS_Crypto_00211]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Activity diagram: Length checks and length adjustment during partial copying. Both size checks lead to the same return value, so their order is irrelevant. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00207" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00207">[SWS_Crypto_00207]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00208" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00208">[SWS_Crypto_00208]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00209" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00209">[SWS_Crypto_00209]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00210" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00210">[SWS_Crypto_00210]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00211" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00211">[SWS_Crypto_00211]</a></p>
<p>The following functions are available for the generation and derivation of key material:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyGenerate</code> generates new key material <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91007">[SWS_Crypto_91007]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyDerive</code> derives a key into <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91008">[SWS_Crypto_91008]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_RandomSeed</code> feeds the seed <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91013">[SWS_Crypto_91013]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal</code> calculates its own public value for key exchange <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91009">[SWS_Crypto_91009]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret</code> stores the shared secret as an element of the same key <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91010">[SWS_Crypto_91010]</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_7_2_Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_7_2_Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 84</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Asymmetric key material is passed in standardized formats. The actual extraction of the elements is then handled by the driver <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_5_Key_Formats.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_5_Key_Formats">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 28</a>:</p>
<table>
<thead><tr><th>Key type</th><th>Format according to R20-11</th><th>Reference</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Asymmetric with identifier</td><td>RFC5958/ASN.1, <code>CRYPTO_KE_FORMAT_BIN_IDENT_PRIVATEKEY_PKCS8</code></td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00184" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00184">[SWS_Crypto_00184]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>RSA</td><td>RFC 8017, OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00185" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00185">[SWS_Crypto_00185]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00186" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00186">[SWS_Crypto_00186]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00187" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00187">[SWS_Crypto_00187]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00188" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00188">[SWS_Crypto_00188]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>ECC (NIST, Brainpool)</td><td><code>CRYPTO_KE_FORMAT_BIN_OCTET</code>; public X|Y, private X|Y|Scalar, little endian</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00189" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00189">[SWS_Crypto_00189]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00190" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00190">[SWS_Crypto_00190]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00191" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00191">[SWS_Crypto_00191]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>ED25519</td><td>public X, private seed K|X, little endian</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00192" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00192">[SWS_Crypto_00192]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00193" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00193">[SWS_Crypto_00193]</a></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h4>Key State and Persistence in NvM</h4>
<p>Each key is either valid or invalid:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Crypto_KeySetValid</code> sets it to valid <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91014">[SWS_Crypto_91014]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_KeySetInvalid</code> sets it to invalid <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91020">[SWS_Crypto_91020]</a>.</li>
<li><code>Crypto_KeyGetStatus</code> returns the current state <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>According to the change history, the functions for querying and invalidating the key state were added with R20-11 <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_General_Overview.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_General_Overview">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 2</a>. If a key is invalid, services such as <code>Crypto_KeyGenerate</code> or <code>Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret</code> return the value <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_5_2_Crypto_KeyGenerate.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_5_2_Crypto_KeyGenerate">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 80</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_7_2_Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_3_4_7_2_Crypto_KeyExchangeCalcSecret">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 84</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">State diagram: Transitions between valid and invalid as well as invalidation during startup. The initial state after successful loading is not specified in the references and is therefore not shown. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91014">[SWS_Crypto_91014]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91020">[SWS_Crypto_91020]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91019">[SWS_Crypto_91019]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00198" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00198">[SWS_Crypto_00198]</a></p>
<p>The handling of key elements in the NvM is also new in R20-11 <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_General_Overview.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_General_Overview">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 2</a>. A key references at most one NvM block, and its KeyType comprises one or more KeyElements <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-756a92d11d252023.html" data-snip="FIG-756a92d11d252023">AUTOSAR_SWS_CryptoDriver p. 32</a>. The driver writes the elements during validation and reads them during initialization <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_NVM_SECTION_7_2_6_Key_Storage_in_NVM.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_NVM_SECTION_7_2_6_Key_Storage_in_NVM">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 35</a>. Version R25-11 clarifies that only KEYSETVALID triggers storage, but not <code>Crypto_KeyElementSet</code>. This allows the driver to verify interdependent elements together and save them in a single write operation <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_6_1_Writing_keys_to_NVM.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_6_1_Writing_keys_to_NVM">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 37</a>.</p>
<p>The driver provides four callbacks for data exchange with the NvM:</p>
<ul>
<li>Init initializes the block <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91023" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91023">[SWS_Crypto_91023]</a>.</li>
<li>ReadFrom copies from the NvM mirror into the internal buffer <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91024" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91024">[SWS_Crypto_91024]</a>.</li>
<li>WriteTo fills the mirror shortly before writing <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91025" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91025">[SWS_Crypto_91025]</a>.</li>
<li>Callback reports the end of an asynchronous single block request <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91026" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91026">[SWS_Crypto_91026]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Optionally, the driver uses <code>NvM_SetRamBlockStatus</code> and <code>NvM_WriteBlock</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91017" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91017">[SWS_Crypto_91017]</a>.</p>

<h4>Cancellation of Running Jobs</h4>
<p><code>Crypto_CancelJob(objectId, job)</code> is synchronous and reentrant, though not for the same Crypto Driver Object <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>. The return value depends on the processing state:</p>
<ul>
<li>If the driver is currently not processing the job, it returns <code>E_OK</code> without further processing <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00214" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00214">[SWS_Crypto_00214]</a>.</li>
<li>If it can cancel a running job, it removes it and returns <code>E_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>.</li>
<li>If it cannot cancel it, for example due to hardware limitations, it returns <code>CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00183" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00183">[SWS_Crypto_00183]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>"In processing" means here that the object is actively busy with the job. A job for which only FINISH is pending is not considered as in processing <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 25</a>. To <code>CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED</code>, the CSM reacts with a cancellation at the next suitable step and reports it via a negative closing callback <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface">SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 80</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Activity diagram: The three outcomes of a cancellation request. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00122">[SWS_Crypto_00122]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00183" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00183">[SWS_Crypto_00183]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00214" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00214">[SWS_Crypto_00214]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface">SWS_CryptoServiceManager p. 80</a></p>

<h4>Behavior in the event of an error</h4>
<p>If development error detection is active, the driver reports the following codes to the DET: <code>CRYPTO_E_UNINIT</code> (0x00), <code>CRYPTO_E_INIT_FAILED</code> (0x01), <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> (0x02), <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> (0x04), <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_VALUE</code> (0x05), as well as a code for buffers that are too small <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00040" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00040">[SWS_Crypto_00040]</a>. These codes are not returned via the API <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_6_Requirements_Tracing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_6_Requirements_Tracing">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 15</a>. An example is <code>Crypto_KeySetValid</code>: Without initialization, it reports <code>CRYPTO_E_UNINIT</code> and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00196" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00196">[SWS_Crypto_00196]</a>. In case of an invalid <code>cryptoKeyId</code>, it reports <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00197" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00197">[SWS_Crypto_00197]</a>. The same pattern applies, for instance, to <code>Crypto_KeyElementCopyPartial</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00205" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00205">[SWS_Crypto_00205]</a> and to <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code> in case of <code>Crypto_KeyDerive</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00180" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00180">[SWS_Crypto_00180]</a>.</p>
<p>Before each job, the driver checks <code>job-&gt;cryptoKeyId</code> and, if applicable, <code>targetCryptoKeyId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00217" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00217">[SWS_Crypto_00217]</a>. For <code>CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE</code>, the destination must always lie within the valid range <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00202" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00202">[SWS_Crypto_00202]</a>. If a buffer is too small, the driver does not execute the operation. With DET active, it reports <code>CRYPTO_E_SMALL_BUFFER</code>; without DET, it returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00195" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00195">[SWS_Crypto_00195]</a>. For <code>CRYPTO_HASH</code> and <code>CRYPTO_MACGENERATE</code>, a result truncated to the most significant bits is output instead <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00065">[SWS_Crypto_00065]</a>. The newer document reference additionally mentions <code>CRYPTO_RANDOMGENERATE</code>. This is not substantiated by the present R20-11 requirements <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_4_Error_detection.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_4_Error_detection">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 49</a>.</p>
<p>The driver reports runtime results via return values such as <code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>, and <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_91018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_91018">[SWS_Crypto_91018]</a>. When entropy is exhausted, the random service returns <code>CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED</code>. <code>Crypto_ProcessJob</code> then additionally reports the runtime error <code>CRYPTO_E_RE_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00141" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00141">[SWS_Crypto_00141]</a>. For NvM errors, there is <code>CRYPTO_E_RE_NVM_ACCESS_FAILED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Crypto_00194" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Crypto_00194">[SWS_Crypto_00194]</a>. However, the application must handle defective NvM blocks <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_NVM_SECTION_7_2_6_Key_Storage_in_NVM.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_NVM_SECTION_7_2_6_Key_Storage_in_NVM">SWS_CryptoDriver p. 35</a>.</p>
